verdict.statement: The service saw these digests under these names at the seal's time, after the previous seal. A seal does not show that the files are correct; it is not a qualified time-stamp.
The network operator vetted this station and its position. An attestation says who may feed as attested data; it does not show that the station's observations are true.

evidence.finding: GNSS signal levels stayed normal for this installation throughout
The reported positions disagree with observations that do not depend on the vessel's GNSS
The AIS broadcast departs from the onboard GNSS receiver, whose positions agree with the independent observations
Regional monitoring reported no interference near the platform at the time
The reported track jumps faster than a vessel can move (2 jumps)

limits: MODELLED: rules checked on synthetic episodes with known cause; not validated on a labelled set of real incidents
An engineering reconstruction of the data supplied, not a legal finding; intent is not assessed
Receiver logs supplied by the platform's operator are only as trustworthy as their chain of custody
Missing data is never degraded; low coverage is itself a source of basis risk.
An episode at one station that nearby stations with normal data did not share is excluded as uncorroborated.
The index measures signal degradation at the stations; it is not a measure of any insured party's loss.
verdict.statement: An outage index and a trigger state under the stated definition. Not insurance or financial advice, not a claim decision, not a payout calculation and not an interpretation of any policy wording.
